note: Release notes shown in the update prompt and the What's new panel. Newest first. Edit this file only — src/data/changelog.ts imports it and re-fetches it from the network so a stale tab can name the build it is about to receive.

releases.title: Strength of Materials joins the by-topic drills

changes.text: A sixth by-topic subject: Strength of Materials, 227 items across eight sections — simple stresses, axial deformation, torsion, shear and moment, flexure, combined loadings, thin-walled pressure vessels and Mohr's circle. Pick a section, or several, and sit as many items as you want from each.

The drawings come with it. Most of these situations read off a figure rather than the prose — a span, an eccentricity, a cross-section, an angle on a failure plane — so each one is reproduced as a panel cut from the scanned page, dimension labels and all.

No answer key yet. The booklet prints problems only, so every Strength item gets the same treatment Physics has: it opens, it takes your answers and your ratings, but nothing is marked right or wrong until the key is published. A sitting with no key does not record a score.

releases.title: Multiplayer (beta) — sit a paper with other people

changes.text: Multiplayer is in beta. Rooms are run by the host's browser rather than a server, so a result is practice, not a record — nothing from a room reaches the leaderboards.

A Multiplayer section of its own. Host a room and get a four-character code, or browse the public rooms already waiting. Codes never use 0, O, 1, I, L, 5 or 2, so one read out loud cannot be mistyped.
Co-op: everyone shares one paper and scatters across the items. A choice needs the most picks to become the team's answer — an even split leaves the item unanswered rather than guessing.
Versus: the same paper, separate scores. The palette marks the items your opponent has already answered, without revealing what they picked.

Surprise me randomises a drill's topics and items, or picks a paper at random within the area you chose. Physics is left out of multiplayer until its key is printed, because an unkeyed paper cannot be scored.
Results show everyone's profile and score, and in Co-op a celebration banded by the team's percentage. Reaction GIFs — cats and dogs first — can be sent live and appear above the sender's card.

Every item now has a Report button beside Flag, in the by-topic drills and in the Gillesania and Besavilla sittings for MSTC, HPGE and PSAD. Pick what is wrong — key, wording, figure, solution — and add a note if you want.
The report travels with the item as you saw it: stem, choices, figure caption and booklet page, so the admin can find it without asking you to retype anything.
Admins get a Question Reports queue that keeps the count of items still open, and can mark a report reviewing, fixed or dismissed with a note of what changed.

releases.title: Fluid Mechanics drills are now scored

changes.text: Fluid Mechanics is marked: the booklet's printed key for all 148 items is in, so pressure, plane and curved surfaces, buoyancy, dams, metacenter and rigid-body motion now come back right or wrong.
Update notices now say what changed before you reload, and a What's new panel keeps the history.
90 Physics items across eight topics, from rectilinear and projectile motion through forces and gravitation to work, energy and momentum.
Ten Physics figures cropped from the booklet, sized so a tall diagram no longer pushes the answer choices off the screen.

releases.title: Leave a drill and come back to it

changes.text: Leaving a drill now asks whether to keep it. Unfinished drills and finished ones are listed in their own panel beside the topic picker.
Statics is keyed — all 176 items, across forces, equilibrium, frames, friction and cables.
The topic picker no longer pre-selects a subject, so a drill is always one you chose.
Powers and roots were printing as escape codes, so "4 cm³/sec" arrived as a jumble of letters and digits.
Calculus figures 40 and 41 were cropped through the drawing; both were re-cut.
Differential equations item 126 asked for a reading at 110° without saying half a minute.

releases.title: Analytics, ratings and the Fluent 2 skins

changes.text: Performance analytics built from your own stored answers, with topic mastery weighted by how hard you rated each item.
Rate any item easy, mid or hard; hard items come back more often in the next draw.
The two Fluent 2 skins lead the theme picker, with glass, gradient and pointer-driven depth.
A by-topic drill no longer reports itself as a board sitting.
